R0801.summary: Branislav Žarković is a Full Professor at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, with demonstrated expertise in credit risk and SME finance. His work centers on credit scoring for thin-file and micro-enterprise borrowers, alternative/open banking data for underwriting, explainable AI in credit decisions, and regulatory implications of machine learning in lending. He also has practical banking experience as a former head of risk, which informs his applied research orientation.

expertise.topic: Credit scoring for thin-file and micro-enterprise borrowers
Alternative data and open banking for lending decisions
Explainable and interpretable credit risk models
Regulatory and compliance implications of AI and credit models
SME finance and credit access in transition markets

R0995.summary: Veljko Pantelić (R0995) is an Assistant Professor in Computing and Control Engineering whose work centers on software engineering for industrial automation, especially model-driven and domain-specific tooling for IEC 61131-3 PLC software. His record shows sustained expertise in metamodeling, code generation, software product lines, DSL design, and safety-aware automation software, with both academic and applied industry-facing work.

expertise.topic: IEC 61131-3 PLC metamodeling and Structured Text tooling
Model-driven engineering and model-to-text / code generation for PLC software
Software product lines and variability management in industrial automation
Domain-specific language design and IDE support for industrial control programming
Safety-aware automation software and industrial PLC validation

R0919.summary: Martina Lačoková (R0919) is a Senior Research Associate in computing and control engineering whose work centers on software engineering for embedded and real-time systems, especially testing and formal methods for automotive and industrial CAN-based integration. Her record shows sustained expertise in combinatorial interaction testing, interface contracts, runtime monitoring, compositional verification, and tool-supported contract derivation for multi-supplier embedded stacks.

expertise.topic: Combinatorial interaction testing and constrained covering arrays for embedded/automotive systems
Interface contract specification and contract-based integration for CAN/CAN FD and AUTOSAR systems
Runtime verification and low-overhead monitoring for embedded CAN systems
Formal methods and compositional verification for embedded software stacks
Automotive and industrial embedded integration testing in multi-supplier environments

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on contract-driven generation of CAN integration tests for multi-supplier AUTOSAR stacks at DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.
proposal.problem: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. currently reaches 87–89% branch coverage before shipment, yet three of the last four delivered projects still had CAN communication faults discovered during customer integration testing. The recurring issue is boundary behavior between components from different suppliers: each part conforms to its own specification, but their interaction fails when connected. The company has ARXML descriptions, COM configuration, and a CANoe environment, but no systematic method to generate tests that target the assumptions one component makes about another. The goal is to develop a contract-based testing method and supporting tooling that reads existing AUTOSAR descriptions and produces test scenarios aimed at interface contracts between suppliers, with practical use inside DriveLogic’s current project workflow.
research_questions: Can interface contracts for multi-supplier AUTOSAR/CAN components be derived automatically from ARXML, COM configuration, and existing interface descriptions with sufficient precision to guide test generation?

Can constrained covering-array based test generation improve detection of cross-supplier CAN interaction faults compared with DriveLogic’s current manually designed integration tests while staying within the company’s existing CANoe-based workflow?
Can the resulting generated tests be executed with low enough setup and maintenance effort to fit a company process that currently uses LDRA, CANoe/CANalyzer, and customer toolchains?

plan.work: Map DriveLogic’s current AUTOSAR/CAN integration artifacts to a formal contract model; define fault classes for cross-supplier interaction bugs; build a prototype that extracts test-relevant parameters and constraints from ARXML and COM configuration; prepare a first test-generation pipeline that targets the company’s existing CANoe environment.
plan.result: A validated contract model for one representative project and a prototype generator that produces candidate integration tests from real project descriptions.
plan.pass_if: On one selected DriveLogic project, the prototype extracts at least 90% of the agreed test-relevant interface parameters from ARXML/COM artifacts and generates at least 20 candidate tests that company engineers judge as executable in CANoe with only minor adaptation.

plan.work: Extend the prototype to constrained covering-array generation for interface assumptions and interaction faults; compare generated tests with the company’s current manually written integration tests on historical or ongoing project data; refine the contract rules based on feedback from DriveLogic engineers.
plan.result: A repeatable method for generating focused integration tests and an evidence set showing which interaction faults are covered by the generated suite.
plan.pass_if: The generated suite detects at least one realistic cross-supplier interaction fault in a pilot evaluation or, if no live fault is available, matches or exceeds the fault-revealing power of the company’s existing test set on at least one historical case study while staying within the same execution budget.

plan.work: Package the method as a lightweight workflow for DriveLogic, including documentation and a reusable tool chain; validate maintenance effort when components or supplier interfaces change; prepare industrial dissertation results and publication material with company review.
plan.result: A deployable testing workflow for contract-driven CAN integration testing and a defended industrial PhD thesis with documented industrial validation.
plan.pass_if: DriveLogic can apply the workflow to at least one evolving project with no more than one engineer day of adaptation per interface change, and the final evaluation shows clear reduction in uncovered interaction-risk cases relative to manual test design.

proposal.company_brings: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. brings a real industrial setting in Novi Sad, 27 employees, AUTOSAR Classic integration expertise, existing CAN, LIN and Ethernet stack work, ARXML descriptions, COM configuration, CANoe, LDRA-based coverage reports, and the ability to dedicate one senior engineer part-time, roughly 40% of their working week, to a collaborative research activity tied to active projects.
proposal.faculty_brings: Martina Lačoková brings expertise in combinatorial interaction testing, interface contract specification, runtime monitoring, compositional verification, and tool-supported contract derivation for CAN-based embedded systems, together with access to the Faculty of Technical Sciences environment and its CAN/LIN bus laboratory and small cluster for constraint-solving workloads.
proposal.why_this_pair: This pair matches the problem closely: DriveLogic’s challenge is about unseen interaction faults at supplier boundaries in AUTOSAR/CAN integration, and Martina Lačoková’s work directly covers contract-based integration testing, constrained covering arrays, and runtime verification for multi-supplier embedded stacks. The company can supply real project artifacts and an execution environment, while the researcher can supply the formal and algorithmic methods needed to turn those artifacts into targeted tests.
proposal.novelty: The project goes beyond Martina Lačoková’s closest prior work by turning her published methods on constrained covering arrays and interface contracts into an operational industrial workflow for a real AUTOSAR integration setting. Relative to SYN-PUB-09743, the novelty is not only generating minimum-size covering arrays for constrained parameter spaces, but doing so from industrial ARXML and COM artifacts for supplier-boundary faults. Relative to SYN-PUB-09744 and SYN-PUB-03011, the novelty is not only specifying or deriving contracts, but using them directly to generate executable CANoe test scenarios for a specific company process. Relative to SYN-PUB-09748, the novelty is in maintenance and evolution of generated tests inside a live industrial workflow rather than only incremental maintenance of test suites in the abstract. Relative to SYN-PUB-09749 and SYN-PRJ-0434, the novelty is a focused industrial PhD at DriveLogic with evaluation against the company’s actual 87–89% branch-coverage workflow and recurring post-delivery CAN faults. The closest publication set is therefore SYN-PUB-09743, SYN-PUB-09744, SYN-PUB-09748, SYN-PUB-09749, SYN-PUB-03011, and SYN-PRJ-0434.
proposal.data_status: DriveLogic already has ARXML descriptions of all components in the project, the COM configuration, the CANoe environment, and LDRA coverage reports showing 87–89% branch coverage before shipment. The company also reports that in the last four delivered projects, three had CAN communication faults found during customer integration testing. What still needs to be collected for the research is a structured corpus of representative interface descriptions, selected historical or ongoing integration cases, examples of supplier-boundary faults, and a labeled set of contract assumptions and expected behaviors for at least one pilot project. No claim is made here that historical fault data is already organized for research use; that collection and labeling would be part of the project setup.
proposal.first_step: Next month, agree on one pilot AUTOSAR/CAN project at DriveLogic, gather its ARXML, COM configuration, and existing CANoe test assets, and run a joint workshop to identify the first set of interface assumptions and recurring boundary-fault patterns to encode into the prototype.
proposal.to_agree: Funding for the candidate and the split between university supervision time and DriveLogic engineer time; whether DriveLogic pays any part of the candidate’s industrial salary or project costs; access conditions for ARXML, COM, CANoe, and any historical integration-fault evidence; IP ownership for new tooling, generated tests, and derived contract models, including background IP from both sides; publication delay and review window before submission of papers or the dissertation; and the exact scope of data that can be stored, anonymized, and reused beyond the pilot project.

final.title: Industrial PhD on contract-driven generation of CAN integration tests for multi-supplier AUTOSAR stacks at DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.
final.problem: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. currently reaches 87–89% branch coverage before shipment, yet three of the last four delivered projects still had CAN communication faults discovered during customer integration testing. The recurring issue is boundary behavior between components from different suppliers: each part conforms to its own specification, but their interaction fails when connected. The company has ARXML descriptions, COM configuration, and a CANoe environment, but no systematic method to generate tests that target the assumptions one component makes about another. The goal is to develop a contract-based testing method and supporting tooling that reads existing AUTOSAR descriptions and produces test scenarios aimed at interface contracts between suppliers, with practical use inside DriveLogic’s current project workflow.
research_questions: Can interface contracts for multi-supplier AUTOSAR/CAN components be derived automatically from ARXML, COM configuration, and existing interface descriptions with sufficient precision to guide test generation?

Can constrained covering-array based test generation improve detection of cross-supplier CAN interaction faults compared with DriveLogic’s current manually designed integration tests while staying within the company’s existing CANoe-based workflow?
Can the resulting generated tests be executed with low enough setup and maintenance effort to fit a company process that currently uses LDRA, CANoe/CANalyzer, and customer toolchains?

plan.work: Map DriveLogic’s current AUTOSAR/CAN integration artifacts to a formal contract model; define fault classes for cross-supplier interaction bugs; build a prototype that extracts test-relevant parameters and constraints from ARXML and COM configuration; prepare a first test-generation pipeline that targets the company’s existing CANoe environment.
plan.result: A validated contract model for one representative project and a prototype generator that produces candidate integration tests from real project descriptions.
plan.pass_if: On one selected DriveLogic project, the prototype extracts at least 90% of the agreed test-relevant interface parameters from ARXML/COM artifacts and generates at least 20 candidate tests that company engineers judge as executable in CANoe with only minor adaptation.

plan.work: Extend the prototype to constrained covering-array generation for interface assumptions and interaction faults; compare generated tests with the company’s current manually written integration tests on historical or ongoing project data; refine the contract rules based on feedback from DriveLogic engineers.
plan.result: A repeatable method for generating focused integration tests and an evidence set showing which interaction faults are covered by the generated suite.
plan.pass_if: The generated suite detects at least one realistic cross-supplier interaction fault in a pilot evaluation or, if no live fault is available, matches or exceeds the fault-revealing power of the company’s existing test set on at least one historical case study while staying within the same execution budget.

plan.work: Package the method as a lightweight workflow for DriveLogic, including documentation and a reusable tool chain; validate maintenance effort when components or supplier interfaces change; prepare industrial dissertation results and publication material with company review.
plan.result: A deployable testing workflow for contract-driven CAN integration testing and a defended industrial PhD thesis with documented industrial validation.
plan.pass_if: DriveLogic can apply the workflow to at least one evolving project with no more than one engineer day of adaptation per interface change, and the final evaluation shows clear reduction in uncovered interaction-risk cases relative to manual test design.

proposal.title: Industrial PhD on plain-language explanations for automated SME credit decisions at Kredo Fintech
proposal.problem: Kredo Fintech needs a compliant explanation format for automated credit decisions that a borrower can understand and challenge, in Serbian and, for planned expansion, Macedonian. Its current gradient-boosted scoring model performs well, and SHAP is already used internally, but the existing explanation summary is too technical for borrowers and not yet satisfactory for compliance. The solution must be generated automatically at decision time, stored with the decision record, and work reliably in production within about six months, while fitting Kredo Fintech’s modest budget and existing lending workflow.
research_questions: How can feature-level model explanations be translated into plain-language borrower explanations that remain faithful to the decision logic while being understandable to non-technical micro- and small-business borrowers?

Which explanation template and wording strategy best satisfies the needs of borrowers and compliance for automated credit decisions in Serbian, with a maintainable path to Macedonian, when tested on Kredo Fintech’s live decision flow?
What minimum set of explanation elements can be generated automatically at decision time and stored with the decision record without degrading model performance or operational latency in production?

plan.work: Map the current decision workflow, explanation needs, and compliance constraints; review the existing SHAP-based internal summary; define the explanation schema and borrower-facing language principles; build a prototype that turns model outputs into plain-language Serbian explanations.
plan.result: A validated explanation specification and first prototype integrated into a test version of the decision flow.
plan.pass_if: A prototype explanation can be generated automatically for at least 95% of test decisions, is stored with the decision record, and passes an internal review by Kredo Fintech’s compliance officer and data team against a predefined checklist.

plan.work: Run iterative testing with real decision cases from Kredo Fintech; compare at least two explanation variants for clarity, challengeability, and regulatory fit; refine Serbian wording and prepare the Macedonian version of the template.
plan.result: A tested explanation template set in Serbian, with a translation-ready Macedonian structure, plus documented performance and usability findings.
plan.pass_if: At least 80% of tested borrowers or internal reviewers rate the chosen explanation as understandable, and the explanation adds no more than a small, agreed latency to decision-time generation in the test environment.

plan.work: Deploy the selected explanation format in production; monitor stability, complaint/challenge patterns, and operational handling; document the final method and academic results for the industrial PhD thesis.
plan.result: A production-ready explanation module and thesis-ready evidence on explainable SME credit decisions in a regulated fintech setting.
plan.pass_if: The production system generates compliant explanations for live automated decisions for three consecutive months without critical failures, and Kredo Fintech confirms the format can support the North Macedonia rollout.

proposal.company_brings: Kredo Fintech brings an active automated SME lending platform, a 26-person team, a data team of five, the current gradient-boosted scoring model, existing SHAP-based internal summaries, decision records, and practical constraints from regulated lending in Novi Sad. It also brings a real deployment context for Kredo SME Loans, Kredo Flex Line, Kredo Score Report, and Kredo Portal, with the need to render explanations in Serbian and later Macedonian.
proposal.faculty_brings: Branislav Žarković brings expertise in credit scoring for thin-file and micro-enterprise borrowers, alternative data and open banking for lending decisions, explainable and interpretable credit risk models, and regulatory implications of AI and credit models, supported by his publications on scoring micro-enterprises with little credit history, explaining credit decisions to supervisors, alternative data in consumer credit scoring, explainability requirements under the EU AI Act, and benchmarking scorecard interpretability metrics. He also brings industrial PhD supervision experience and practical banking insight from being a former head of risk at a regional bank.
proposal.why_this_pair: This pair matches a live regulatory problem with a researcher who has direct, relevant experience in credit explainability and SME lending. Kredo Fintech needs a production-ready explanation layer for automated lending, and Branislav Žarković’s work already addresses credit decisions, explainability, alternative data, and regulatory expectations. The company can supply real decision cases and operational constraints; the researcher can turn those into a defensible method that works in production.
proposal.novelty: The closest prior work is SYN-PUB-08747, 'Explaining credit decisions to supervisors: a case study,' together with SYN-PUB-08751, 'Explainability requirements under the EU AI Act: implications for credit scoring vendors.' This industrial PhD goes beyond those publications by converting explainability from supervisor-facing analysis into borrower-facing, production-grade text generation tied to decision-time deployment, decision storage, and bilingual delivery for Serbian and Macedonian. It also extends the research from general compliance discussion to a tested explanation template embedded in a live fintech workflow.

proposal.to_agree: They still need to agree the funding package for the industrial PhD, including who pays for the candidate’s time and any company staff time beyond the data team of five; access rules for decision records and any personal or sensitive data; background IP and ownership of new explanation code, templates, and thesis results; publication delay for company review; and whether Macedonian implementation will be included in the initial scope or reserved for a later phase.

proposal.problem: AutomVoj a.d. has 38 active PLC codebases for customer installations, all written in ladder logic in TIA Portal, and a safety-related patch currently takes three engineers two full weeks because each codebase must be found, adapted, and tested separately. The practical problem is to introduce modular reuse and structured change management without rewriting the installed base at once, so that future safety patches can be propagated faster and with less manual effort.
research_questions: Can a variability model be built for the 38 active PLC codebases that captures the stable common parts and the customer-specific differences with enough precision to support patch propagation?
Can safety-related changes be applied incrementally so that a patch can be generated or guided for each affected codebase without full regeneration or a full rewrite?
Can the proposed approach reduce the current effort from three engineers for two full weeks per patch cycle to a repeatable process that AutomVoj can maintain during live project work?

plan.work: Inventory a representative subset of the 38 active codebases, identify recurring ladder-logic patterns, and derive a variability model and common library structure that fits AutomVoj's existing TIA Portal practice. Use the PLC laboratory at the Faculty of Technical Sciences for small validation cases and compare the model against actual customer variants.
plan.result: A first reusable model of shared logic and customer-specific variation points, plus a validated subset of candidate reusable components for ladder logic in TIA Portal.
plan.pass_if: At least 10 codebases are analysed; at least 6 recurring logic patterns are documented; and the model can explain at least 80% of the selected differences in the analysed subset.

plan.work: Develop an incremental patching workflow that maps one safety change into the variant model and then into the affected codebases, with tests that can be run on representative installations. Validate the workflow on a patch scenario similar to the emergency-stop sequence change described by AutomVoj.
plan.result: A prototype process for propagating safety changes across multiple PLC codebases without rewriting each one from scratch.
plan.pass_if: A single safety change can be applied to at least 5 codebases through the workflow, and the required engineering effort is reduced to no more than one engineer for one week for the prototype case.

plan.work: Harden the approach on AutomVoj's real maintenance flow, refine the library and model based on engineer feedback, and document a maintenance process that can be used by the chief engineer and senior automation engineers without special research support.
plan.result: A maintainable reuse and patching method for the installed base, together with thesis results and company-ready guidelines.
plan.pass_if: The approach is demonstrated on at least 12 codebases, and AutomVoj can describe a repeatable process that its team can carry out without the doctoral candidate for a full patch cycle.
